column1: # Python package versions that shipped malware. One line each, tab separated.
# After editing, run: bash tools/gen.sh
#   name      the package as its .dist-info folder spells it in site-packages (litellm-1.107.0.dist-info)
#   version   the exact version (every version, *, is not supported)
#   incident  an id from data/incidents.tsv, whose level must be act
#   os        all, mac, linux or win: where the version's malware could run, as its advisory says. The
#             version is looked for on every OS; on one where its malware could not run, the report
#             shows it as a version to update, not a compromised machine. none: the package's own
#             maintainer says the version's malware could not run (the level rule in data/bad-npm.tsv's
#             header), so it is a version to update on every OS
# Each line is looked for as a .dist-info folder in every Python environment found and as a
# name-version entry in uv's cache. Section 5 shows one row per incident, named as incidents.tsv names it.
# mistralai 2.4.6 is Linux-only by Mistral's advisory. guardrails-ai 0.10.1, published in the same wave
# (Wiz), is linux by the code SafeDep's post on the TanStack wave recovered from it: it runs only when
# sys.platform starts with linux, writes /tmp/transformers.pyz, the file Mistral lists, and runs it.
# The maintainer's advisory, GHSA-xmpw-2vmm-p4p6, names no OS; Wiz and Socket (the project's issue
# 1473) read it as Linux-only too. That file has a line for each of the two in data/indicators.tsv.
# lightning 2.6.2 and 2.6.3, the PyPI release of April's Mini Shai-Hulud wave (Wiz), start a credential
# stealer when imported, on any OS (GitHub's malware advisory GHSA-g4wr-mm54-799x); Lightning AI's own
# advisory (GHSA-w37p-236h-pfx3) says to assume the environment is compromised and to pin 2.6.1. No
# source names a file they leave on the machine; the files their payload commits to a repository are in
# data/planted.tsv.
# litellm 1.82.7 and 1.82.8, March 2026: OpenSSF's MAL-2026-2144 (the entry that also names 1.107.0) and
# GitHub's GHSA-5mg7-485q-xm76, on any OS; LiteLLM's own post says they stole credentials and that
# 1.82.8 also carried litellm_init.pth, its file in data/indicators.tsv.
# durabletask 1.4.1 to 1.4.3, May 2026: GitHub's malware advisory GHSA-3qf7-886j-9wrc and OpenSSF's
# MAL-2026-4174; its dropper runs when imported on Linux only, and the advisory says to treat a Linux
# system that imported one as fully compromised. Wiz ties it to the AntV wave (data/bad-npm.tsv): the
# account that published that wave's repositories took the PyPI token from microsoft/durabletask-python.
# It is its own incident, since the AntV wave's is an npm incident. Its files are in data/indicators.tsv.
# telnyx 4.87.1 and 4.87.2, March 2026: Telnyx's own advisory, GHSA-955r-262c-33jc, and GitHub's malware
# advisory GHSA-crmv-hqwr-fqfv (OpenSSF's MAL-2026-2254). Telnyx says 4.87.1's typo kept its malware
# from running, so it is a version to update (none), and that 4.87.2's ran on Linux, macOS and Windows.
# Telnyx ties it to the LiteLLM compromise of March by the same RSA key; it is its own incident.
# pytorch-lightning 2.6.2 and 2.6.3 have no line: Lightning AI's advisory, GHSA-w37p-236h-pfx3, gives
# that name in its package field, but its text says only one of our PyPI packages, the maintainers'
# thread on the compromise (Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning issue 21691) speaks of lightning, which is
# listed, and neither PyPI nor deps.dev knows a pytorch-lightning 2.6.2 or 2.6.3: no source shows
# that they were published.
